key_insight: Two scale-invariant spectral heuristics help characterize QAOA mixer topologies, but their agreement with performance depends on the cost structure.
engineering_relevance: These metrics offer topology-aware guidance for mixer selection beyond convention and circuit constraints, while highlighting the need to assess mixer–cost alignment.
method: Measure normalized minimum eigenvalue separation of the mixer Hamiltonian.
Measure long-time averaged minimum eigenvalue separation of the mixer unitary.
Derive exact expressions and asymptotic bounds for complete graphs, hypercubes, cycles, and balanced 2-D tori.
evidence_signal: Empirical QAOA performance broadly follows the spectral characterization for random permutation-invariant costs, but not for structured 1-D and 2-D Ising QUBOs.
watch_item: These cost-agnostic heuristics do not guarantee QAOA performance; structured problems can require mixer–cost alignment.
paper_title: Quantum-Walk Inspired Spectral Metrics for Evaluating QAOA Mixers
